title: Menu balance
summary: How to spread prices between cheap, medium and expensive items, and how to display them.

sections.heading: Omnes' four rules
items: Price proportionality: the most expensive item costs up to 2 or 3 times the cheapest. A business can't be expensive and cheap at the same time.
Item proportionality: the medium price zone has as many items as the cheap and expensive zones combined.
Fit between offered and demanded prices: the average ticket must be within ±10% of the average menu price.
Fit with the customer's budget: the daily special goes in the medium price zone.

sections.heading: Price or product strategy
paragraphs: If you compete on price, list prices in a column on the right of the menu: customers focus on the price.
If you compete on product, place the price as close as possible to the dish description: it has less psychological impact.
